AFD WUI applies only within Full Purpose and Limited Purpose Jurisdiction; ETJ parcels are exempt from WUI but defer to the applicable county ESD for fire access.

     9→## Authoritative sources

Submittals with original submission date before July 10, 2025 governed by 2021 IFC. Appendix D **not** adopted — apparatus access is governed by LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503–507.5 with local amendments.

    16→- **Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM):** §§ 7.3, 7.5 (driveways serving fire lanes); ASMP Street Network Map for street-level lookup.
    17→- **Hydrant flow data:** AFD hydrant flow test report (Fire Marshal-witnessed; ≤1 year old). Fire Flow Map "Box" number on AW General Info & Construction Notes Sheet.
    18→- **WUI map:** 2024 WUI Code Map (dark blue/teal = Zones A & B combined; light blue = Zone C). Map does not distinguish A from B — AFD Wildfire Division field-measures.
    19→
    20→## Regulatory pathway
    21→
    22→Fire review runs **concurrently** with civil/site plan review through Development Services Department, but AFD has independent sign-off authority. Plans with fire lines additionally require both AFD and DSD approval before Austin Water Processing and Evaluation (AWPE) will approve (UCM 2.5.1.D).
    23→
    24→- **Pre-application:** AFD pre-app meeting strongly advisable for high-rise, podium, mixed-construction, WUI, alternative-surface fire lanes, or any site requiring an AMOC. AFD will not issue AMOC approval numbers during site plan cycle — AMOC must be a **separate standalone submittal**, approved before site plan submission.
    25→- **AMOC track (IFC § 104.8):** Required when standard IFC requirements cannot be met — most commonly to reduce minimum commercial fire flow below 1,500 gpm (floor: 1,000 gpm), reduce hydrant coverage, or approve pyrophoric gas storage. AMOC must be pre-approved with an AFD-issued approval number and date noted in the AFD Fire Analysis Table. "Pending"/"submitted" entries are deficient.
    26→- **WUI track (FPCM 4.10.0):** Concurrent review by AFD Wildfire Division. Required for any property within Full/Limited Purpose Jurisdiction that the 2024 WUI Code Map covers or that AFD Wildfire designates. Separate WUI approval stamp required before final site plan approval. Map status is rebuttable only by AFD Wildfire Division — self-declared "not in WUI" is a deficiency.
    27→- **High-rise track (IBC § 202 via LDC § 25-12-1):** Any occupied floor >75 ft above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access triggers IBC § 403 high-rise requirements: Fire Command Center (1-hr fire barrier; exterior access or 2-hr rated passageway; FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.13 equipment list), dual remote FDCs (NFPA 14 § 7.12.2), fire pump room, dual water mains (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.e), AEDs each occupied level, simultaneous stairway-unlock controls (LDC § 25-12-173 § 508.1.6). For buildings >420 ft, mains must be in **different streets** (IFC § 914.3.1.2). Buildings between ~65–75 ft must carry three pre-CO survey notes (ZLU-29.10/.11/.12).
    28→- **Decision body:** Fire Marshal's office; Wildfire Division (for WUI); final sign-off on cover sheet approval block.
    29→- **Timeline reality:** AMOC review adds ~6–12 weeks before site plan submission becomes viable. WUI concurrent review rarely controls the critical path. High-rise pre-app + dual-main coordination with Austin Water can add 1–2 cycles. Any post-approval change to fire lanes, hydrants, FDCs, fire service routing, riser/pump rooms, or electric disconnect requires AFD resubmission.
    30→
    31→## Constraints to evaluate
    32→
    33→**Apparatus access (LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503.1.1, 503.2.1, 503.2.4 with City amendments; Appendix D not adopted).**
    34→- Fire apparatus access road within **150 ft** (path-of-travel, not arc) of all portions of all exterior walls of the first story. AFD routinely extends to **200 ft** for buildings fully sprinklered per NFPA 13 (not 13R/13D) under Exception 1.1, but the increase is **discretionary** — plans showing 200 ft must reflect AFD authorization; high-piled combustible storage buildings (>12,000 sf area + storage >12 ft height) are locked at 150 ft regardless of sprinklers (IFC § 3206.6). High-piled storage also requires one FD access door per 100 LF of exterior wall facing the access road, max 125 ft center-to-center (IFC § 3206.6.1, § 3206.7.5).
    35→- Measurement: actual ground-level path around obstructions ≥4 ft tall (buildings, walls, fences, grade changes); never through/under buildings; never across water-quality features; AFD will not lay supply hose across ASMP Level 3+ arterials, expressways, parkways, freeways, or toll roads. Routes that cross property lines require a recorded **JUAE or UDA** (§ 503.1.1 Exception 3).
    36→- **Minimum unobstructed width 25 ft** face-of-curb to face-of-curb (sidewalk does not count); 14 ft minimum vertical clearance for the full width; **inside turning radius 25 ft / outside 50 ft** (§ 503.2.4). Wider than 25 ft lanes may reduce to 20-in/40-out. Divided fire lanes where aerial is not anticipated: two 15-ft lanes (Exception 2.d). Security gates: 25 ft two-way / 15 ft one-way (20 ft two-way only with prior Fire Prevention Division written approval). Throat at Level 1/2 street crosswalk: 20 ft permitted (Exception 2.e). Curb-return radii at fire-access driveways from public streets follow TCM 7.5.1.1 Table 7-1 "Fire Access" column — typically 15 ft on Level 1/2 streets (vs. 10 ft typical). Turning movements onto opposing traffic lanes or where ASMP proposes a raised median are prohibited.
    37→- **Grade:** asphalt ≤ 13%; concrete ≤ 15%; maximum 10% change in any 20 ft; aerial setup areas ≤ ~12–13% running and 3.5% cross-slope; driveway grade change in a fire lane ≤ 6% (TCM 7.5.2.1.E, more restrictive). Where max grades cannot be met, a fully protected sprinkler system approved by AFD may substitute. Minimum drainage: 2% vegetated / alternative; 1% asphalt; 0.5% concrete.
    38→- **Surface:** HS-20 loading (16 kips/wheel, 80,000 lbs total) for all fire lanes and all structural elements within them (manhole covers, vault lids, trench grates). Final asphalt/concrete must be in place before combustible construction begins. Alternative surfaces (grasscrete, pavers, PICP, porous asphalt/concrete) limited to ≤25% of building-perimeter fire protection, require slip-resistant surfaces at turns and 40 LF at building corners for aerial operations, reinforced mountable curb when no Type I/II apron is present, and a post-completion PE-of-record concurrence letter (§ 503.2.3.1). Pervious or decorative paving **within 100 ft of any building** requires AFD approval + PE design for 80,000 lb live load even when not formally a fire lane.
    39→
    40→**Aerial apparatus (LDC § 25-12-173 § 503.2.6.1; AFD operational practice).**
    41→- Aerial-clearance review begins at ~73 ft per AFD practice (2 ft before the 75-ft high-rise threshold). For high-rise and near-high-rise buildings, plans must demonstrate clear staging adjacent to the building face — typically a 25-ft setback envelope plus overhead clearance for the boom. Divided 15-ft lanes are not permitted where aerial deployment is expected; full 25-ft lane required.
    42→- Elevated surfaces (podium slabs, plaza decks) that serve as fire apparatus access must be designed for the greater of IFC § 503.2.6 apparatus loads or IBC § 1607.8.1 live load (LDC § 25-12-3 § 1607.8.2). **Outrigger loads:** **43,200 lbs on one outrigger** or **28,600 lbs each on two adjacent outriggers** at 18-ft center spacing on 24"×24" contact (§ 503.2.6.1). Engineer of record must sign a post-completion concurrence letter. Access hatches, vault covers, and trench grates in the apparatus path must individually carry the 43,200-lb single-outrigger rating.
    43→- Bridges/elevated fire lane crossings: AASHTO HB-17 (or current LRFD) design; load-limit signs at both entrances (§ 503.2.6).
    44→
    45→**Dead-ends and turnarounds.**
    46→- Dead-end fire lane >150 ft requires a turnaround per Standard 901S-2: cul-de-sac with 50-ft unobstructed radius **or** hammerhead/T 25 ft × 80 ft with 10 ft additional clearance and no obstructions over 1 ft (FPCM 4.4.0).
    47→- Turnaround pavement must be marked fire lane on all sides; hose-lay extension from the turnaround counts toward apparatus-to-building distance.
    48→
    49→**Hydrant coverage and spacing (LDC § 25-12-173 § 507.5.1; UCM § 2.9.2.D).**
    50→- Primary hydrant hose-lay to all exterior walls: **400 ft** non-sprinklered (non-R-3/U); **500 ft** for buildings sprinklered throughout per NFPA 13 or 13R; **600 ft** for Group R-3 and U regardless of sprinklers.
    51→- **Second hydrant within 500 ft (600 ft for R-3/U) when required fire flow ≥1,500 gpm; additional hydrants within 1,000 ft when fire flow >2,500 gpm. One hydrant per 1,250 gpm (or fraction).** Multi-hydrant calcs must show all required hydrants flowing simultaneously, starting at the most hydraulically remote.
    52→- **Spacing:** **300 ft** maximum interval in commercial/high-density areas (CBD, DMU, W/LO, CS, CH, MF-4/5/6, or inside the Downtown Austin Project Coordination Zone); **600 ft** max interval elsewhere; hydrant at every major intersection; hydrants on **both sides** of any divided road regardless of arterial class (UCM 2.9.2.D.2).
    53→- **Placement (SSM 511.4.B):** 3–6 ft behind curb gutter face; steamer center ≥18 in above grade; steamer perpendicular to and facing the curb/fire lane; ≥20 ft from curb tangency at corners; ≥9 ft (any direction) from sanitary sewer line/lateral/service/manhole (UCM 2.9.2.D.4); ≥5 ft from storm drain; ≥3 ft clear circumference; bollards where exposed to vehicles; lead line ≤55 ft from main and cannot cross a divided road.
    54→- **Field-verified fire flow test:** AFD-conducted or AFD-witnessed only (IFC § 507.4 as locally amended); ≤1 year old at site-plan submission; on hydrants on the same main/zone serving the connection point; full FPCM Appendix E § 2.4.0 data set (static, residual, pitot, flow rate, hydrant IDs, date/time, conductor, equipment, gauge elevations).
    55→- **Required fire flow at 20 psi residual** from IFC Appendix B Table B105.1(2) using IBC construction type + fire-flow calculation area per LDC § 25-12-173 B104.1. Commercial floor: 1,500 gpm (reducible to 1,000 gpm only with pre-approved AMOC). Sprinkler reductions per Table B105.2: NFPA 13 → 75%; NFPA 13R → 50% (capped at 50% for Type III/IV/V); NFPA 13D → 25%. **No reduction** for Group H or S-1/S-2 with high-piled or rack storage.
    56→- Hydraulic calc C-factors are fixed by FPCM 4.4.0 Table 507-2: C=80 (iron/steel) or C=110 (plastic/copper) — software defaults of 140/150 are non-compliant. **Velocity ≤10 fps** upstream of the 6-in hydrant tap; the 6-in lead downstream is the only velocity exception.
    57→
    58→**FDC siting (IFC § 912; LDC § 25-12-173 § 912.5; NFPA 14 § 6.4.5.4).**
    59→- Each separate sprinkler or standpipe system requires its own FDC (NFPA 13D excluded; stand-alone local <20-head systems excluded per FPCM 4.7.0). Street side, oriented to fire apparatus access, fully visible. Prohibited: under building overhangs, inside parking garages (even sprinklered), behind walls/fences, in 100-yr floodplain, in covered courtyards.
    60→- **FDC-to-hydrant travel distance:** **100 ft** for standpipe systems (NFPA 14 § 6.4.5.4); **300 ft** for sprinklered buildings without Class I standpipe (IFC § 507.5.1.1). Working space: 36 in W × 36 in D × 78 in H; mounting 18–48 in above grade.
    61→- High-rise: minimum **two remotely located FDCs** on separate building walls as far apart as possible (NFPA 14 § 7.12.2). For multi-zone standpipe systems, at least two FDCs per zone. FDC pressure demand ceiling: **150 psi** non-high-rise / **350 psi** high-rise (FPCM 4.8.0).
    62→- Austin-amended FDC sign: white reflective letters on red, "FDC" ≥6 in tall, other words ≥2 in, approved text strings only ("FDC", "AUTOMATIC SPRINKLERS", "STANDPIPES", "TEST CONNECTION", combinations) — "FIRE DEPARTMENT CONNECTION" is **not** an approved string. Manual standpipes must indicate "MANUAL" + "WET"/"DRY"; PRV-equipped systems indicate floor range served.
    63→
    64→**Fire area and high-rise classification.**
    65→- Fire-flow calculation area = total gross floor area of all stories, mezzanines, basements, mechanical, and parking levels under exterior walls and horizontal roof projections (LDC § 25-12-173 B104.1). Exceptions: Type IA/IB → three largest successive floors (construction-type-based, **not** high-rise-based); open parking garage of IA/IB per IBC § 406.5 → single largest floor; R-3/R-4/townhouse/1–2-family separated <10 ft → combined.
    66→- Fire walls per IBC § 706 create separate fire areas **only with zero openings**. Any fire door, damper, or utility penetration disqualifies the separation.
    67→- Podium exclusion of garage from upper fire area (IBC § 510.2) requires **both** a 3-hr fire-rated horizontal assembly with no openings **and** NFPA 13 (not 13R) in the garage.
    68→- High-rise threshold: any occupied floor >75 ft above the lowest level of fire department vehicle access (lowest finished grade of any adjacent fire lane / street; sloped sites use the downhill side). Standpipe trigger: highest floor >30 ft above same datum (IFC § 905.3.1). NFPA 13R disallowed for buildings ≥4 stories or with highest occupied floor ≥30 ft above lowest FD access (IFC § 903.3.1.2).
    69→- Aerial-apparatus clearance review begins at ~73 ft per AFD operational practice — design overhead, planter, and side-yard clearances accordingly.
    70→
    71→**WUI (LDC § 25-12-183).** Proximity Zones A (≤50 ft from ≥40 ac wildland), B (>50 ≤150 ft), C (>150 ft ≤0.5 mi from ≥40 ac, or within 1.5 mi of ≥750 ac). Most restrictive zone applies to the entire structure when it spans multiple zones. ETJ exempt.
    72→
    73→**Underground fire main + utility interface (UCM 2.9.2.B.6; NFPA 13/24).**
    74→- Service from public main to property line: **ductile iron** (DI); gate valve at the tap to the public main; backflow preventer inside property line, accessible for City inspection; **flow detection device** on every unmetered fire line, positioned so ≤100 gallons sit between the device and the public main.
    75→- **NFPA 13 minimum fire service main: 6 in** (NFPA 13 § 24.1.3.1); smaller permitted only with PE-sealed hydraulic calc from a TX-licensed RME sprinkler designer. **Underground may extend ≤10 ft under building** (NFPA 13 § 10.4.3.1; NFPA 24 § 10.6.1); >10 ft triggers trench requirements (rigid walls, noncombustible base, accessible from within, drain, restrained joints, shutoff valve, freeze protection).
    76→- Sectional control valves required when the private fire main serves **≥7 fire-protection connections** (NFPA 24 § 6.6.1). Each private hydrant gets a gate valve at the tee, restrained to the main with bolt-through connection (UCM 2.9.2.C.1). Fully restrained joints throughout (UCM 2.9.2.D).
    77→- **NFPA 13 exterior shutoff** (NFPA 13 § 8.16.1) — one of: underground PIV ≥40 ft from building; wall-mounted PIV; exterior door direct to riser room within 15 ft walking distance (not under overhang); BFP vault (no hydrants downstream of BFP, no PIV upstream of BFP, no other valves in vault). PIVs not required for NFPA 13R/13D.
    78→- High-rise fire pumps require **two water main connections** with independent supply piping each sized for full pump demand (UCM 2.9.2.A.3.e). Same-main exception only with valving between tap points. Buildings >420 ft: connections must be in **different streets** (IFC § 914.3.1.2). Parallel supply mains require ≥10 ft separation.
    79→
    80→**Knox Box / Knox Switch (FPCM 4.4.0; FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.16; IFC § 506.1).**
    81→- Knox Key Box required for any commercial structure with fire-protection systems (sprinklers, alarm, standpipe) **or** any site with physical access barriers (locked gates, fenced perimeters, bollards). Knox is the only approved brand in Austin. Must be called out on plans with a specific leader-line — a general note is insufficient.
    82→- **Knox Key Switch** (electrical, not a key vault) required for any motorized/power-operated gate on a fire apparatus access road, ingress side. Substituting a Knox Box for a Switch at a motorized gate is deficient.
    83→- High-rise: additional Knox Key Box per FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.13(A.5), distinct from the riser-room Knox Box.
    84→
    85→**Construction-phase fire protection (IFC § 3313; FPCM 4.4.0 General Note 3).**
    86→- When combustible materials arrive on site, **≥500 gpm within 500 ft** must be available (IFC § 3313). For Type I/II construction, vertical work may proceed once this supply is in place, ahead of full permanent fire flow.
    87→- Required fire-protection infrastructure (mains, private hydrants, apparatus roadways) must be installed and operational before any combustible/vertical construction begins (IFC § 501.4). Final asphalt or concrete on apparatus access surfaces must be in place before combustible construction begins.
    88→- Existing hydrants and FDCs must remain in service through all phases; replacement hydrants must be accepted as operational before the existing hydrant they replace is removed. Modifications to private fire mains require advance email notification to FirePrevention@austintexas.gov (IFC § 901.7.4) and return-to-service notice (§ 901.7.6).
    89→
    90→**Pipeline ordinance (LDC §§ 25-4-134, 25-2-516).** Two-prong test: hazardous liquid per 49 CFR § 195.2 **AND** ≥8-in inside diameter. Natural gas (49 CFR Part 192) does not qualify. AFD Fire Analysis Table field must read "YES" when a qualifying pipeline is on or adjacent to the site.
    91→
    92→## Opportunities to evaluate
    93→
    94→- **NFPA 13 sprinklers → 75% fire-flow reduction** (cap by post-reduction floor of 1,000 gpm). Often unlocks a workable supply scenario on sites with marginal Box-number capacity. For Type III/IV/V wood-frame construction, NFPA 13R is capped at 50%; pushing to non-combustible (II-B) construction can unlock the full 75% reduction.
    95→- **AMOC to drop the commercial minimum to 1,000 gpm** (FPCM Appendix D). Viable for small commercial buildings where the standard 1,500-gpm floor would otherwise force a new tap or main upsize. Must be approved before site plan submission — budget 6–12 weeks.
    96→- **Podium construction (IBC § 510.2)** excludes the garage from upper-fire-area calcs and can drop fire flow by a tier — but requires 3-hr horizontal assembly with no openings **and** NFPA 13 in the garage, which costs more than NFPA 13R-throughout in soft sites.
    97→- **200-ft sprinklered apparatus access (Exception 1.1)** is AFD-routine for NFPA 13 buildings and meaningfully expands the buildable envelope on sites where a 150-ft constraint would force unnecessary internal drives or rated breezeways.
    98→- **Rated breezeway** (2-hr fire-rated walls + ceiling, full sprinkler, open both ends, 14-ft clearance, required signage) can satisfy apparatus access for landlocked rear-of-building exterior points where a perimeter loop is infeasible.
    99→- **Alternative-surface fire lanes** (grasscrete, PICP, pavers) preserve open-space and water-quality goals but capped at 25% of building perimeter fire protection and require PE concurrence — useful for compact urban infill but rarely sufficient as the primary route.
   100→- **Limited area wet pipe (NFPA 13 § 4.2)** for freestanding R-2 amenity buildings (clubhouses, leasing offices) in 13R projects — avoids forcing a full NFPA 13 design on an otherwise unsprinklered ancillary structure (FPCM 4.4.0).
   101→- **Bureau programs:** check `bureau/jurisdictions/austin/programs/` for any AFD expedited-review or pre-approved-typology programs that may apply.

   103→## Inputs needed from Phase 2
   104→
   105→- **wwp.md** — Fire Flow Map Box number; AFD hydrant flow test report (≤1 yr, AFD-conducted/witnessed) with static/residual/flow and AWWA-projected available flow at 20 psi; existing hydrant locations and IDs within 500 ft; whether an SER is anticipated; existing main sizes/materials.
   106→- **transportation.md** — ASMP Street Level of all frontages (governs apparatus turning radii per TCM Tables 7-1/7-2 and the "no hose lay across major roadway" rule); adjacent ROW widths; presence of medians/divided roadways; driveway approach geometry.
   107→- **zoning.md / sde.md** — Base zoning district (drives 300 vs. 600 ft hydrant spacing); DAPCZ status; setback envelope (controls apparatus-to-building distance feasibility); building height envelope (drives 30-ft standpipe and 75-ft high-rise triggers).
   108→- **phase1-extraction/concept-plan-data.md** — Building footprints, story count, highest occupied floor elevation, IBC construction type assumption, fire-flow calculation area per building, intended occupancy classifications, gate locations, parking-garage open/enclosed determination, podium configuration if any.

   111→## Output structure
   112→
   113→Standard discipline output shape per `references/phase3-disciplines.md`. Include the AFD Fire Analysis Table fields as a structured findings table — IFC edition (governed by **original** submission date), construction type, high-rise Yes/No (with the 75-ft datum), fire area (with calc method), IWUIC edition + Proximity Zone, AMOC status, pipeline-ordinance Yes/No — because Phase 4 will lift these into the diligence report.

   115→## Severity heuristics
   116→
   117→| Finding | Severity |
   118→|---|---|
   119→| Required fire flow (post-sprinkler reduction) exceeds AWWA-calculated available flow at 20 psi — capacity upgrade (new tap, main upsize, SER, or storage tank + fire pump) required | `significant` |
   120→| Building >75 ft above lowest FD access without dual-main supply, fire pump, FCC, or required high-rise envelope — concept needs redesign or alternative procurement track | `significant` |
   121→| Property in WUI Zone A or B without site-design accommodation (defensible space, ignition-resistant exterior, modified setbacks); or qualifying hazardous pipeline triggers buffer/easement constraint | `significant` |
   122→| Aerial apparatus required (highest occupied floor approaching 75 ft) but setbacks, overhead clearances, or HS-20 setup pads don't accommodate it | `significant` |
   123→| Apparatus access path-of-travel exceeds 200 ft to one or more exterior building points on a sprinklered building, or >150 ft non-sprinklered, with no rated-breezeway or second-passage option | `significant` |
   124→| Fire-area calc method depends on Type IA/IB classification, podium § 510.2 exclusion, or fire-wall separation that materially changes required fire flow tier — design margin is thin | `moderate` |
   125→| AMOC needed to clear commercial 1,500 gpm floor (down to 1,000 gpm) — schedule risk of 6–12 weeks pre-submittal | `moderate` |
   126→| Dead-end aisle >150 ft without turnaround, or cul-de-sac/hammerhead geometry below 901S-2 spec | `moderate` |
   127→| Hydrant nominally beyond required spacing but workable with new tap on existing main; second-hydrant trigger at 1,500 gpm not yet addressed | `moderate` |
   128→| Cross-property fire access requires a JUAE/UDA not yet recorded | `moderate` |
   129→| Alternative-surface fire lane proposed for >25% of perimeter, or pervious paving within 100 ft of buildings without AFD PE-design pathway | `moderate` |
   130→| Standard commercial/multifamily occupancy with adequate hydrant coverage, NFPA 13 sprinklers, and apparatus access within standard envelope | `note` |
   131→| AFD General Notes verbatim from FPCM § 4.4.0; AFD Fire Analysis Table complete with correct IFC edition for original submission date | `note` |

   133→## Common pitfalls
   134→
   135→- **Citing IFC Appendix D for apparatus access** — Austin does not adopt Appendix D. Access is governed by LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503–507.5 with local amendments.
   136→- **Using the wrong IFC edition.** Original submission date governs, not resubmittal: 2012 IFC (pre 1/7/18) → 2015 IFC → 2021 IFC (9/1/21–7/9/25) → **2024 IFC (7/10/25 onward).** FPCM Appendix D still internally references 2012 IFC; LDC governs.
   137→- **Substituting the Fire Flow Map Box nominal value for an AWWA-calculated available flow** at 20 psi from actual AFD test data. The Box is a modeled value; the calculated flow must come from the test.
   138→- **Confusing high-rise (height) and Type IA/IB (construction type).** Three-largest-floors fire-area exception is **construction-type-based**. A Type IIIA high-rise does not get it; a Type IA low-rise does.
   139→- **NFPA 13R applied to a 4-story or ≥30-ft-occupied-floor building** — disallowed; full NFPA 13 required (IFC § 903.3.1.2). The 30-ft datum is the lowest level of fire department vehicle access, not average grade or primary entry.
   140→- **Assuming the 200-ft sprinklered access distance is automatic.** It is a discretionary increase by the fire code official; high-piled storage buildings (>12,000 sf + >12 ft storage) are locked at 150 ft.
   141→- **Hose-lay measured as straight-line, arc, or through a water-quality pond.** Path of travel only, around obstructions ≥4 ft tall, never across major arterials/expressways/parkways/freeways/toll roads, never diagonally across intersections.
   142→- **Self-declaring "not in WUI."** Only AFD Wildfire Division determines applicability and Proximity Zone, regardless of map status. ETJ parcels are exempt.
   143→- **AMOC entered as "pending" or "submitted"** in the AFD Fire Analysis Table — must be an AFD-issued approval number and date from a separate, prior, standalone submittal.
   144→- **C-factor 140 or 150** in private fire-main hydraulic calcs (software defaults). Required: C=80 iron/steel; C=110 plastic/copper/resin-lined (FPCM 4.4.0 Table 507-2).
   145→- **Hydrants placed within 9 ft of any sanitary sewer** (any direction) or in/within 6 in of a sidewalk/ramp — both are common SSM 511.4.B / UCM 2.9.2.D.4 fails.
   146→- **Mistaking a natural-gas pipeline for a "hazardous pipeline."** The ordinance requires hazardous liquid under 49 CFR Part 195 **and** ≥8-in ID. Natural gas (Part 192) does not qualify.
   147→- **ETJ parcels: ESD authority.** Within Travis County (ESD #2), Hays County, Williamson County, or city limits of Buda etc., AFD does not govern — confirm the correct fire authority before applying any Austin-specific rule.
   148→- **Knox Box in a general note only.** FPCM Appendix E § 3.2.16 requires a specific leader-line callout with location and size; a plan note saying "Knox Box to be provided" is deficient.
   149→- **"IFC 503.3.3.2" cited on plans.** This section does not exist in Austin's adopted code; correct authority for fire-zone marking is FPCM 4.4.0 General Construction Notes and LDC § 25-12-173 § 503.3.2.
   150→- **Fire lane labels on water utility easement drawings.** Fire-zone designation is exclusively AFD jurisdiction (§§ 503.3, 503.1.4); placing fire-lane labels on AW utility easement plats implies utility-department enforcement and is a deficiency.
   151→- **Bare "IFC" terminology in fire-flow demand tables.** UCM 2.9.2.A.3.b requires "City of Austin Fire Code" terminology, with "City of Austin Local Amendments" attached to every IFC section citation.
   152→- **AFD General Notes modified from FPCM § 4.4.0 verbatim language** or augmented with Knox Box specs or non-AFD jurisdictions (Travis County ESD #2, etc.) — must be exact FPCM text, six notes only.
   153→- **AFD Fire Analysis Table combined with the Austin Water Project Information Table.** Must be a standalone table on the cover sheet with nine required left-column fields verbatim (FPCM § 4.4.0).
   154→- **Treating the Fire Flow Zone Box number as the available flow.** The Box reflects modeled capacity; available flow at 20 psi must be AWWA-calculated from actual AFD test data, and the two values must reconcile on plans.
   155→- **Fire main interconnected with domestic supply or backed up by a domestic meter.** Prohibited (NFPA 13 § 16.9.3.1); cross-connection protection by reduced-pressure backflow assembly is required (IFC § 507.6 as locally amended).

# Fire Findings — 12713 Cinchring Ln

**Property:** 12713 Cinchring Ln, Austin, TX 78727 — Lot 12, Block M, Scofield Subdivision
**Proposed use:** Demolish existing SFR; build ground-up duplex (2 units)
**Lot:** ~7,840 sq ft (0.18 acres), SF-2 zoning
**Jurisdiction:** City of Austin, Full Purpose — Austin Fire Department
**Applicable code:** 2024 International Fire Code (adopted via LDC § 25-12-171, Ord. 20250410-039, effective July 10, 2025); building construction governed by IRC (International Residential Code) for duplex (Group R-3 occupancy)

---

## Summary

- **Low overall fire-code risk.** A two-unit duplex built under the IRC on an existing platted lot within a developed suburban subdivision presents a straightforward fire profile with no high-rise, standpipe, NFPA 13, or commercial fire-flow triggers.
- **WUI status is very likely non-applicable.** The site is in a flat, fully urbanized 1990s subdivision with no adjacent wildland; web research and wildfire risk tools indicate low risk. Formal confirmation from AFD Wildfire Division is still required — self-declaration is not accepted.
- **Fire apparatus access is satisfied by existing public street.** Cinchring Ln is a public residential street providing frontage; a two-story duplex footprint well within 150 ft of the street requires no private fire lane, turnaround, or AMOC.
- **Hydrant coverage benefits from the 600-ft R-3 allowance.** Group R-3 occupancies receive the most generous hose-lay distance (600 ft) regardless of sprinkler status. Existing subdivision hydrant infrastructure almost certainly satisfies this, but the nearest hydrant location should be field-verified.
- **Sprinklers are not required** for an IRC duplex unless the building exceeds specific IRC thresholds (e.g., fire area, access limitations). No NFPA 13/13R/13D system is anticipated; no FDC, fire pump, or standpipe applies.

---

## Findings

### 1. Governing Code Edition

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | LDC § 25-12-171; Ord. 20250410-039 |
| **Finding** | The 2024 IFC is effective for submittals with an original submission date on or after July 10, 2025. This project, targeting submission in 2026, falls under the 2024 IFC. The duplex itself is constructed under the IRC, not the IBC, as a Group R-3 two-family dwelling. |
| **Implication** | Plans and any fire-related notes must reference the 2024 IFC and applicable City of Austin local amendments. Using the 2021 IFC edition would be a deficiency. |
| **Recommended next step** | Ensure the permit application and plan sheet notes cite the correct code edition (2024 IFC, IRC for building construction). |

### 2. Fire Apparatus Access

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | LDC § 25-12-173 §§ 503.1.1, 503.2.1 |
| **Finding** | Cinchring Ln is an existing public residential street providing direct frontage to the lot. All exterior walls of a duplex on a ~7,840 sq ft lot will be within 150 ft path-of-travel from the street. No private fire apparatus access road, fire lane, or turnaround is required. The project does not trigger aerial apparatus review (max height 35 ft, well below the 73-ft threshold). |
| **Implication** | No fire lane design, HS-20 loading analysis, or turnaround geometry is needed. No AMOC for apparatus access distance. |
| **Recommended next step** | No action required. Confirm during plan review that the building footprint does not extend beyond 150 ft from the nearest point of fire apparatus access on Cinchring Ln. |

### 3. Hydrant Coverage

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | data-gap |
| **Citation** | LDC § 25-12-173 § 507.5.1; UCM § 2.9.2.D |
| **Finding** | Group R-3 and Group U occupancies receive a 600-ft hose-lay allowance to all exterior walls, regardless of sprinkler status. Hydrant spacing in non-commercial/non-high-density areas (SF-2 qualifies) is 600 ft maximum interval. Scofield Subdivision, developed in the 1990s, has existing hydrant infrastructure. However, the exact location of the nearest hydrant and its distance to the proposed building have not been field-verified. |
| **Implication** | If an existing hydrant is within 600 ft hose-lay of all exterior walls (highly likely in a developed subdivision), no new hydrant or tap is required. No fire flow test is anticipated for an IRC duplex that does not trigger sprinkler or commercial fire-flow requirements. |
| **Recommended next step** | Field-verify or confirm via Austin Water GIS the location of the nearest fire hydrant and measure hose-lay distance to the farthest exterior wall of the proposed duplex. |

### 4. Fire-Flow Demand

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | IRC; IFC Appendix B Table B105.1(2) (informational for R-3) |
| **Finding** | An IRC duplex (Group R-3, two-family dwelling) does not trigger the commercial fire-flow analysis pathway under the IFC. Fire flow for one- and two-family dwellings is governed by the IRC and the local jurisdiction's residential water supply standards. Austin Water's existing mains in Scofield Subdivision serve the existing SFR and are expected to be adequate for a replacement duplex of comparable scale. |
| **Implication** | No AFD fire flow test, no AWWA available-flow calculation, and no fire-flow demand table are required for permit. No AMOC for fire-flow reduction is needed. |
| **Recommended next step** | No action required beyond standard Austin Water tap plan review for the new duplex service connections. |

### 5. Sprinkler / Fire Suppression System

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | IRC R313; IFC § 903 |
| **Finding** | Austin has not adopted a residential sprinkler mandate for IRC one- and two-family dwellings beyond the IRC's own thresholds. A standard two-story duplex does not trigger NFPA 13, 13R, or 13D requirements. No standpipe is required (building height well below 30 ft above lowest FD access). No FDC is required. |
| **Implication** | No sprinkler design, FDC siting, fire pump, or riser room is needed. This eliminates significant cost and design complexity. |
| **Recommended next step** | None. If the developer voluntarily installs sprinklers (e.g., for insurance benefits), NFPA 13D would be the applicable standard for a two-family dwelling. |

### 6. Building Separation / Fire-Resistance Between Units

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | moderate |
| **Citation** | IRC R302.1, R302.2, R302.3 |
| **Finding** | The zoning pathway confirms that HOME Phase 1 imposes no zoning-based building separation requirement for duplex units. However, the IRC requires fire-separation construction between dwelling units in a duplex: a 1-hour fire-resistance-rated wall assembly from foundation to underside of roof sheathing (IRC R302.2), with no plumbing or mechanical penetrations that compromise the rating. Exterior wall fire-resistance and opening protection depend on fire-separation distance from the property line (IRC R302.1 Table R302.1). |
| **Implication** | The architect/designer must detail the party wall (or floor/ceiling assembly if stacked units) to meet IRC fire-separation requirements. This is standard duplex construction but must be explicitly shown on plans. Exterior walls within 3 ft of a property line require 1-hour rating with no openings; walls 3-5 ft require 1-hour rating with limited openings. The 5-ft side setback on this lot will govern the exterior wall treatment. |
| **Recommended next step** | During design, confirm fire-separation distance from each side property line and detail the party wall and any exterior walls within 5 ft of a property line for IRC R302.1 compliance. |

### 7. Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) Status

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | data-gap |
| **Citation** | LDC § 25-12-183; FPCM 4.10.0; 2024 WUI Code Map |
| **Finding** | Web research indicates Scofield Farms is in a flat, fully urbanized, suburban area with no adjacent wildland of 40+ acres. The area is classified as low wildfire risk. The property is almost certainly outside WUI Zones A, B, and C. However, per Austin's fire feasibility requirements, only AFD Wildfire Division can make the official WUI determination — self-declaration of "not in WUI" is a deficiency. |
| **Implication** | If confirmed outside WUI, no ignition-resistant construction, defensible space, or WUI-specific review applies. If unexpectedly within WUI Zone C (the outermost zone), additional exterior material requirements would apply but would not materially affect project feasibility. |
| **Recommended next step** | Check the 2024 WUI Code Map via Austin GIS to confirm the property is not within any WUI zone. If any ambiguity, request a written determination from AFD Wildfire Division before permit submission. |

### 8. Knox Box

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | FPCM 4.4.0; IFC § 506.1 |
| **Finding** | Knox Box is required for commercial structures with fire-protection systems or sites with physical access barriers. A standard IRC duplex without sprinklers, fire alarm, or gated access does not trigger the Knox Box requirement. |
| **Implication** | No Knox Box or Knox Switch is needed. |
| **Recommended next step** | None. |

### 9. Hazardous Pipeline

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | LDC §§ 25-4-134, 25-2-516 |
| **Finding** | No hazardous liquid pipeline (49 CFR Part 195, 8-in+ ID) has been identified on or adjacent to the property. Natural gas service (Texas Gas Service, 49 CFR Part 192) does not qualify under the pipeline ordinance. |
| **Implication** | No pipeline buffer, setback, or AFD Fire Analysis Table "YES" entry is required. |
| **Recommended next step** | None. |

### 10. Construction-Phase Fire Protection

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | note |
| **Citation** | IFC § 3313; FPCM 4.4.0 General Note 3 |
| **Finding** | When combustible materials arrive on site, 500 gpm within 500 ft must be available (IFC § 3313). The existing subdivision hydrant network is expected to satisfy this requirement. The existing hydrant(s) must remain in service throughout demolition and construction. |
| **Implication** | Standard construction-phase requirement; no special infrastructure needed. Contractor must not obstruct or disable existing hydrants during demolition or construction. |
| **Recommended next step** | Confirm nearest hydrant location is within 500 ft of the construction site and ensure it remains accessible throughout the project. |

---

## Open Questions for the Engineer

1. **Nearest hydrant location and distance.** What is the location of the nearest fire hydrant to the proposed duplex, and does the hose-lay path-of-travel to the farthest exterior wall fall within 600 ft? (Field verification or Austin Water GIS confirmation needed.)

2. **WUI map status.** Has the 2024 WUI Code Map been checked for this parcel? If the property appears on the map, has AFD Wildfire Division been contacted for a formal zone determination?

3. **Fire-separation distance at side yards.** With 5-ft side setbacks, will any exterior wall be closer than 3 ft to the property line (e.g., eaves, projections)? This determines whether IRC R302.1 requires a 1-hour-rated exterior wall with no openings versus limited openings.

4. **Party wall construction type.** Has the designer specified the party wall assembly (IRC R302.2 — 1-hour fire-resistance-rated, foundation to underside of roof sheathing, no through-penetrations)? Will the duplex be side-by-side or stacked?

5. **Voluntary sprinklers.** Is the developer considering voluntary NFPA 13D sprinklers for insurance premium reduction or marketability? If so, this would require coordination with Austin Water for a dedicated fire service line and backflow preventer.
